questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. A translation along the transversal t carries line n onto line m. Use this translation to explain why angle 2 = angle 6.
questions.prompt_markup:
In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. A translation along the transversal t carries line n onto line m.
Use this translation to explain why angle 2 = angle 6.
questions.required_method: The translation moves the point where t meets n to the point where t meets m, keeps t on itself, and carries n onto m (they are parallel). So it carries angle 2 onto angle 6. A translation keeps angle measures, so angle 2 = angle 6.

sections.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from congruent angles

questions.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from congruent angles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent. Explain why m and n must be parallel. (Suppose they meet at a point P, and look at the triangle formed with t.)
questions.prompt_markup:
Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent.
Explain why m and n must be parallel. (Suppose they meet at a point P, and look at the triangle formed with t.)
questions.required_method: A complete argument: if m and n met at P, they would form a triangle with t. One of the congruent angles would be an exterior angle of that triangle and the other a remote interior angle. But an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so it is greater than either one. That is a contradiction, so m and n do not meet: they are parallel.
